name: Malaysia
summary: Bank Negara Malaysia licenses and supervises conventional banks under the Financial Services Act 2013 and issues binding policy documents; its Financial Intelligence and Enforcement Department is the FIU under AMLA. Express training duties sit in AMLA section 19 and the 2024 AML/CFT/CPF and TFS policy document, the Fair Treatment of Financial Consumers, Customer Information, Complaints Handling and Product Transparency policy documents, and RMiT, which requires annual cybersecurity awareness. Bank staff dealing in capital market products also face Securities Commission CPE rules, and the Personal Data Protection Commissioner enforces the amended PDPA.

regulators.name: Bank Negara Malaysia
regulators.role: Central bank and prudential and conduct regulator of licensed banks; competent authority under AMLA; issues binding policy documents on AML/CFT, conduct, governance and technology risk.

regulators.name: Financial Intelligence and Enforcement Department, Bank Negara Malaysia
regulators.role: Malaysia's financial intelligence unit; receives suspicious transaction and cash threshold reports from reporting institutions.

regulators.name: Securities Commission Malaysia
regulators.role: Capital market regulator; banks are registered persons for capital market activities, and their employees are subject to SC conduct and CPE rules.

regulators.name: Personal Data Protection Commissioner
regulators.role: Administers and enforces the Personal Data Protection Act 2010, including data protection officer and breach notification duties added in 2024.

regulators.name: Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission
regulators.role: Investigates corruption and enforces the MACC Act, including corporate liability under section 17A.

regulators.name: Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia
regulators.role: Competent authority for FATCA and CRS reporting by Malaysian financial institutions.

regulators.name: Accountant General's Department of Malaysia
regulators.role: Registrar of Unclaimed Moneys; receives balances that banks must transfer under the Unclaimed Moneys Act 1965.

programs.title: Malaysia | AMLA and BNM AML/CFT/CPF Awareness
programs.why: AMLA section 19 makes ongoing employee training a required part of every reporting institution's compliance programme, and the BNM AML/CFT/CPF policy document requires regular awareness and training with refreshers, tailored to each role. Staff who serve customers must be trained before they start, and all staff must know they can be held personally liable. Since March 2026 the amended AMLA also places compliance programme duties on directors, officers and employees personally.

references.title: Policy Document on Anti-Money Laundering, Countering Financing of Terrorism, Countering Proliferation Financing and Targeted Financial Sanctions for Financial Institutions (AML/CFT/CPF and TFS for FIs)
references.note: Banks must run AML/CFT/CPF awareness and training programmes regularly, with refresher courses, pitched to each employee's responsibilities; customer-facing staff must be trained before they deal with customers, and staff must be told they can be personally liable for failures.

references.title: Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (Act 613)
references.note: A reporting institution's compliance programme must include ongoing employee training, such as know-your-customer programmes, and instruction on the duties covering record keeping, suspicious transaction reporting, tipping-off, customer due diligence and record retention.

references.title: Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities (Amendment) Act 2025 (Act A1761)
references.note: Extends the compliance programme and CDD duties to directors, officers and employees personally, lets BNM issue binding instructions on compliance programmes, adds restricted activity (proliferation) financing and a fine of up to RM1 million for breaches of section 19.

programs.title: Malaysia | Countering Terrorism Financing under AMLA and the BNM Policy Document
programs.why: Malaysia's AML law and the BNM policy document cover terrorism financing alongside money laundering, so the mandatory AML/CFT/CPF training must equip staff to spot TF indicators, apply sanctions screening against the UN and Domestic lists, and escalate suspicions to the compliance officer for reporting to BNM's Financial Intelligence and Enforcement Department.

references.title: Policy Document on Anti-Money Laundering, Countering Financing of Terrorism, Countering Proliferation Financing and Targeted Financial Sanctions for Financial Institutions (AML/CFT/CPF and TFS for FIs)
references.note: Banks must run AML/CFT/CPF awareness and training programmes regularly, with refresher courses, pitched to each employee's responsibilities; customer-facing staff must be trained before they deal with customers, and staff must be told they can be personally liable for failures.

references.title: Policy Document on Anti-Money Laundering, Countering Financing of Terrorism, Countering Proliferation Financing and Targeted Financial Sanctions for Financial Institutions (AML/CFT/CPF and TFS for FIs)
references.note: Banks must keep the UN and Ministry of Home Affairs Domestic lists of terrorism-linked designees in a sanctions database, screen customers and transactions against them, and freeze or block matches.

references.title: Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (Act 613)
references.note: A reporting institution's compliance programme must include ongoing employee training, such as know-your-customer programmes, and instruction on the duties covering record keeping, suspicious transaction reporting, tipping-off, customer due diligence and record retention.

programs.title: Malaysia | Countering Proliferation Financing (CPF) and TFS-PF
programs.why: The 2024 BNM policy document extends the training duty expressly to countering proliferation financing and requires banks to assess PF risk and apply targeted financial sanctions on PF. The AMLA amendment in force from 1 March 2026 adds a restricted activity (proliferation) financing offence, so staff training must now cover PF typologies and sanctions evasion.

references.title: Policy Document on Anti-Money Laundering, Countering Financing of Terrorism, Countering Proliferation Financing and Targeted Financial Sanctions for Financial Institutions (AML/CFT/CPF and TFS for FIs)
references.note: Banks must run AML/CFT/CPF awareness and training programmes regularly, with refresher courses, pitched to each employee's responsibilities; customer-facing staff must be trained before they deal with customers, and staff must be told they can be personally liable for failures.

references.title: Policy Document on Anti-Money Laundering, Countering Financing of Terrorism, Countering Proliferation Financing and Targeted Financial Sanctions for Financial Institutions (AML/CFT/CPF and TFS for FIs)
references.note: Sets screening, database, freezing and reporting duties for targeted financial sanctions relating to proliferation financing.

references.title: Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities (Amendment) Act 2025 (Act A1761)
references.note: Extends the compliance programme and CDD duties to directors, officers and employees personally, lets BNM issue binding instructions on compliance programmes, adds restricted activity (proliferation) financing and a fine of up to RM1 million for breaches of section 19.

programs.title: Malaysia | Customer Due Diligence under AMLA Section 16 and the BNM Policy Document
programs.why: AMLA requires the compliance programme to include know-your-customer training and instruction on the CDD duty in section 16, and the BNM policy document requires customer-facing staff to be trained before dealing with customers. CDD rules for banks sit in paragraph 14A, and since March 2026 the CDD duty also binds directors, officers and employees personally.

references.title: Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (Act 613)
references.note: A reporting institution's compliance programme must include ongoing employee training, such as know-your-customer programmes, and instruction on the duties covering record keeping, suspicious transaction reporting, tipping-off, customer due diligence and record retention.

references.title: Policy Document on Anti-Money Laundering, Countering Financing of Terrorism, Countering Proliferation Financing and Targeted Financial Sanctions for Financial Institutions (AML/CFT/CPF and TFS for FIs)
references.note: Customer-facing staff must be trained before dealing with customers; guidance says all-staff training should cover CDD requirements, and paragraph 14A sets the CDD rules for banking and deposit-taking institutions.

references.title: Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities (Amendment) Act 2025 (Act A1761)
references.note: Extends the compliance programme and CDD duties to directors, officers and employees personally, lets BNM issue binding instructions on compliance programmes, adds restricted activity (proliferation) financing and a fine of up to RM1 million for breaches of section 19.

programs.title: Malaysia | Enhanced Due Diligence for Higher-Risk Customers
programs.why: The BNM policy document requires enhanced CDD for higher-risk customers, including those linked to higher-risk countries, and its guidance says customer-facing staff may be trained on when enhanced CDD applies. No separate EDD course is prescribed, but staff must be competent to apply these measures within the mandatory AML/CFT/CPF training.

references.title: Policy Document on Anti-Money Laundering, Countering Financing of Terrorism, Countering Proliferation Financing and Targeted Financial Sanctions for Financial Institutions (AML/CFT/CPF and TFS for FIs)
references.note: Guidance suggests training staff who establish relationships on when enhanced CDD is needed; paragraphs 14A and 17 set enhanced measures for higher-risk customers and countries.

programs.title: Malaysia | Beneficial Ownership Identification
programs.why: The BNM policy document defines beneficial owners of legal persons and arrangements and requires banks to identify and take reasonable measures to verify them as part of CDD. Staff handling corporate and trust customers need the knowledge to do this, though no stand-alone training is prescribed.

references.title: Policy Document on Anti-Money Laundering, Countering Financing of Terrorism, Countering Proliferation Financing and Targeted Financial Sanctions for Financial Institutions (AML/CFT/CPF and TFS for FIs)
references.note: Defines beneficial ownership and requires identification and verification of beneficial owners of legal persons and legal arrangements during CDD.

programs.title: Malaysia | Politically Exposed Persons under the BNM Policy Document
programs.why: Paragraph 15 of the BNM policy document applies PEP measures to all types of PEPs and their family members and close associates. Staff must be able to recognise PEP relationships and escalate them for senior approval and enhanced monitoring; this is a competence expectation rather than a separate training mandate.

references.title: Policy Document on Anti-Money Laundering, Countering Financing of Terrorism, Countering Proliferation Financing and Targeted Financial Sanctions for Financial Institutions (AML/CFT/CPF and TFS for FIs)
references.note: Sets the requirements for foreign, domestic and international organisation PEPs, including family members and close associates.

programs.title: Malaysia | Sanctions Screening against the UN and Domestic Lists
programs.why: BNM requires sanctions screening of existing, potential and new customers and of transactions against the UN and Domestic lists, regardless of thresholds. Screening and escalation teams need to know the lists, matching and freezing steps; the policy document requires competence but does not prescribe a separate screening course.

references.title: Policy Document on Anti-Money Laundering, Countering Financing of Terrorism, Countering Proliferation Financing and Targeted Financial Sanctions for Financial Institutions (AML/CFT/CPF and TFS for FIs)
references.note: Banks must maintain an up-to-date sanctions database and screen all customers and transactions as part of CDD and ongoing due diligence.

programs.title: Malaysia | Targeted Financial Sanctions: Freezing, Blocking and Reporting
programs.why: Under the BNM policy document, a bank that finds a match must freeze funds or block or reject transactions without delay and report to BNM. Those who operate the controls must understand the procedure; BNM has penalised institutions for TFS breaches.

references.title: Policy Document on Anti-Money Laundering, Countering Financing of Terrorism, Countering Proliferation Financing and Targeted Financial Sanctions for Financial Institutions (AML/CFT/CPF and TFS for FIs)
references.note: Banks must freeze, block or reject on a positive match and report, for terrorism-financing, proliferation-financing and other UN sanctions regimes.

programs.title: Malaysia | Suspicious Transaction Reporting to BNM's FIED
programs.why: AMLA section 19 requires staff to be instructed on the section 14 reporting duty and the section 14A tipping-off ban. The BNM policy document requires prompt suspicious transaction reports to the Financial Intelligence and Enforcement Department regardless of amount, routed internally through branch compliance officers to the head office Compliance Officer.

references.title: Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (Act 613)
references.note: A reporting institution's compliance programme must include ongoing employee training, such as know-your-customer programmes, and instruction on the duties covering record keeping, suspicious transaction reporting, tipping-off, customer due diligence and record retention.

references.title: Policy Document on Anti-Money Laundering, Countering Financing of Terrorism, Countering Proliferation Financing and Targeted Financial Sanctions for Financial Institutions (AML/CFT/CPF and TFS for FIs)
references.note: Banks must promptly report suspicious transactions or attempts, of any amount, to BNM's FIED and set up an internal reporting chain through the Compliance Officer.

programs.title: Malaysia | Correspondent Banking under the BNM Policy Document
programs.why: Paragraph 20 of the BNM policy document sets due diligence, approval and payable-through account requirements for cross-border correspondent banking. Staff managing these relationships must be competent to apply them; no separate training is prescribed.

references.title: Policy Document on Anti-Money Laundering, Countering Financing of Terrorism, Countering Proliferation Financing and Targeted Financial Sanctions for Financial Institutions (AML/CFT/CPF and TFS for FIs)
references.note: Sets requirements for correspondent banking relationships, cross-border arrangements and payable-through accounts.

programs.title: Malaysia | AML/CFT/CPF Risk-Based Approach
programs.why: Banks must apply a risk-based approach, assess ML/TF/PF risks and scale controls accordingly; the policy document's risk guidance lists regular training for directors and employees on ML/TF/PF risks as a possible risk control.

references.title: Policy Document on Anti-Money Laundering, Countering Financing of Terrorism, Countering Proliferation Financing and Targeted Financial Sanctions for Financial Institutions (AML/CFT/CPF and TFS for FIs)
references.note: Requires risk assessment and risk-based controls; the appendix gives regular training on ML/TF/PF risks and typologies as an example of a risk control.

programs.title: Malaysia | AML Record Keeping under AMLA and the BNM Policy Document
programs.why: AMLA section 19 requires employees to be instructed on the record-keeping and retention duties in sections 13 and 17. The BNM policy document requires records to be kept for at least six years, longer if under investigation, in a form admissible in court.

references.title: Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (Act 613)
references.note: A reporting institution's compliance programme must include ongoing employee training, such as know-your-customer programmes, and instruction on the duties covering record keeping, suspicious transaction reporting, tipping-off, customer due diligence and record retention.

references.title: Policy Document on Anti-Money Laundering, Countering Financing of Terrorism, Countering Proliferation Financing and Targeted Financial Sanctions for Financial Institutions (AML/CFT/CPF and TFS for FIs)
references.note: Records from CDD and transactions must be kept up to date, sufficient to reconstruct transactions, and retained for at least six years after the transaction or the end of the relationship.

programs.title: Malaysia | AML/CFT/CPF Training before Dealing with Customers
programs.why: BNM requires employees who deal directly with customers to be trained on AML/CFT/CPF before they deal with any customer, and guidance says their training should cover CDD, ongoing due diligence, enhanced CDD and how to recognise and act on suspicious transactions.

references.title: Policy Document on Anti-Money Laundering, Countering Financing of Terrorism, Countering Proliferation Financing and Targeted Financial Sanctions for Financial Institutions (AML/CFT/CPF and TFS for FIs)
references.note: Customer-facing employees must be trained before serving customers; guidance lists CDD, enhanced CDD and suspicious transaction handling as content for them.

programs.title: Malaysia | AML/CFT/CPF Oversight for the Board and Senior Management
programs.why: Board members must understand their roles in managing ML/TF/PF risks and the AML/CFT/CPF measures required by law, and senior management must understand those risks and provide training to staff. The Compliance Officer must be fit and proper and keep abreast of developments. These are knowledge duties rather than a set course.

references.title: Policy Document on Anti-Money Laundering, Countering Financing of Terrorism, Countering Proliferation Financing and Targeted Financial Sanctions for Financial Institutions (AML/CFT/CPF and TFS for FIs)
references.note: The board must understand ML/TF/PF risks and required measures; senior management must provide training to all levels; the Compliance Officer must be fit and proper and keep up to date.

references.title: Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities (Amendment) Act 2025 (Act A1761)
references.note: Extends the compliance programme and CDD duties to directors, officers and employees personally, lets BNM issue binding instructions on compliance programmes, adds restricted activity (proliferation) financing and a fine of up to RM1 million for breaches of section 19.

programs.title: Malaysia | Anti-Corruption and Adequate Procedures under MACC Act Section 17A
programs.why: Since June 2020 a commercial organisation commits an offence if a director, employee or service provider bribes to win or keep business for it, unless it proves it had adequate procedures; the Minister issues guidelines on those procedures. The guidelines could not be opened (MACC host blocked automated access), so training is treated as part of adequate procedures rather than an express statutory duty.

references.title: Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009 (Act 694)
references.note: Creates corporate liability where an associated person gives gratification for the organisation's benefit, with a defence of adequate procedures to be set out in ministerial guidelines.

references.title: Corporate Liability (Section 17A) guidance
references.note: MACC page on section 17A and the Guidelines on Adequate Procedures; not opened because the host refused automated access.

programs.title: Malaysia | Fraud Awareness for Customer Service Personnel (Unauthorised e-Banking)
audience: Customer service and contact centre staff
programs.why: BNM requires banks to keep customer service personnel well aware of current fraud risks and the bank's end-to-end fraud investigation process so they can advise customers on frauds, scams and identity theft, and to remind customers regularly of safety measures. RMiT adds fraud detection and mule account controls.

references.title: Policy Document on Ensuring Fair Treatment for Victims of Unauthorised e-Banking Transactions
references.note: Customer service personnel must be kept well aware of current fraud risks and the bank's fraud investigation process so they can advise customers on frauds, scams and identity theft; banks must also regularly remind customers of safety tips.

references.title: Policy Document on Risk Management in Technology (RMiT)
references.note: Consolidates earlier e-banking fraud specifications into RMiT, requires secure channels against phishing, and sets fraud detection standards (Appendix 11) covering suspected mule transactions.

programs.title: Malaysia | Corporate Governance under the BNM Policy Document
programs.why: BNM's corporate governance policy document sets board composition, responsibilities, conflicts, culture and disclosure standards, including the board's duty to build the skills it needs. It requires competence rather than a specific course for most staff.

references.title: Policy Document on Corporate Governance
references.note: Requires documented board skill sets, board evaluations and development, and a culture supported by a code of ethics and whistleblowing policy.

programs.title: Malaysia | Director Education and Development (BNM CG and RMiT)
programs.why: Directors must commit to ongoing education and keep a sound understanding of the business and regulatory developments, and the board must fund and maintain development plans for each director. RMiT also requires board members to take part in cybersecurity awareness and training and to receive regular training on technology developments.

references.title: Policy Document on Corporate Governance
references.note: Each director must commit to ongoing education; the board must budget for and maintain development plans so every director has the knowledge and skills needed.

references.title: Policy Document on Risk Management in Technology (RMiT)
references.note: The board must take part in cybersecurity awareness and training and receive regular training on technology developments.

references.title: Policy Document on Fit and Proper Criteria
references.note: When assessing competency of directors and key responsible persons, the board and nomination committee must consider qualifications, training, skills and practical experience; assessments are repeated at least annually.

programs.title: Malaysia | Senior Management Accountability (Responsibility Mapping)
programs.why: From 1 January 2026 banks must map key responsibilities to named senior officers who are fit and proper and competent, and each must acknowledge in writing what they are responsible for. The rule requires competence and clarity of accountability but does not prescribe training.

references.title: Policy Document on Responsibility Mapping
references.note: The CEO must allocate every identified responsibility to a fit and proper senior officer after due diligence on competence, and each member of senior management must give a written acknowledgement of the responsibilities allocated.

programs.title: Malaysia | Fit and Proper Requirements (FSA Section 60)
audience: Senior officers and key responsible persons
programs.why: The Financial Services Act lets BNM set fit and proper criteria covering probity, competency and financial integrity, and the BNM policy document requires assessments that weigh qualifications, training and experience, repeated at least annually.

references.title: Financial Services Act 2013
references.note: BNM may specify fit and proper requirements, including competency and capability, for chairmen, directors, CEOs and senior officers.

references.title: Policy Document on Fit and Proper Criteria
references.note: When assessing competency of directors and key responsible persons, the board and nomination committee must consider qualifications, training, skills and practical experience; assessments are repeated at least annually.

programs.title: Malaysia | Code of Ethics and Fair Treatment Culture
programs.why: Banks must adopt a code of ethics covering confidentiality, conflicts, integrity in reporting and fair treatment, and keep a record of breaches. The fair treatment policy document requires staff, representatives and agents to be trained on the bank's core values and the conduct expected to deliver fair outcomes, with training specific to the role.

references.title: Policy Document on Corporate Governance
references.note: A financial institution must adopt a code of ethics and record and address breaches of it.

references.title: Policy Document on Fair Treatment of Financial Consumers
references.note: Staff, representatives and agents must be trained on the provider's core values and desired conduct; guidance says the training should be role-specific and cover the product lifecycle.

programs.title: Malaysia | Whistleblowing Policy and Channels
programs.why: BNM requires a whistleblowing policy that lets individuals raise concerns in confidence without reprisal, names internal escalation points, and makes individuals aware of external avenues to regulators and law enforcement; the policy must also be communicated to contractors and interns.

references.title: Policy Document on Corporate Governance
references.note: Requires a whistleblowing policy, protection from reprisal, awareness of external avenues, communication to third parties and a designated non-executive director.

programs.title: Malaysia | Personal Liability and Accountability under AMLA and BNM Rules
programs.why: BNM requires banks to make employees aware that they may be held personally liable for failing to observe AML/CFT/CPF requirements. The 2025 AMLA amendment, in force from 1 March 2026, extends compliance and CDD duties and offences to directors, officers and employees personally, and responsibility mapping makes senior officers acknowledge their allocated responsibilities.

references.title: Policy Document on Anti-Money Laundering, Countering Financing of Terrorism, Countering Proliferation Financing and Targeted Financial Sanctions for Financial Institutions (AML/CFT/CPF and TFS for FIs)
references.note: Employees must be made aware that they may be personally liable for failures to observe AML/CFT/CPF requirements.

references.title: Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities (Amendment) Act 2025 (Act A1761)
references.note: Extends the compliance programme and CDD duties to directors, officers and employees personally, lets BNM issue binding instructions on compliance programmes, adds restricted activity (proliferation) financing and a fine of up to RM1 million for breaches of section 19.

references.title: Policy Document on Responsibility Mapping
references.note: The CEO must allocate every identified responsibility to a fit and proper senior officer after due diligence on competence, and each member of senior management must give a written acknowledgement of the responsibilities allocated.

programs.title: Malaysia | Fair Treatment of Financial Consumers (FTFC)
programs.why: The 2024 FTFC policy document, issued under the Financial Services Act, requires banks to embed fair treatment in culture and to train staff, representatives and agents on the core values and conduct needed for fair outcomes across the product lifecycle. It replaced the 2019 version.

references.title: Policy Document on Fair Treatment of Financial Consumers
references.note: Sets the fair treatment outcomes and requires staff, representatives and agents to be trained on core values and desired conduct.

references.title: Financial Services Act 2013
references.note: BNM may set business conduct standards on disclosure, fair terms, promotion, suitability and affordability advice, and complaints handling.

programs.title: Malaysia | Product Transparency and Disclosure
programs.why: BNM's 2024 product transparency policy document requires senior management to ensure that staff and intermediaries who sell or market financial products are adequately trained on the disclosure requirements, with some provisions phased in during 2025-2026.

references.title: Policy Document on Product Transparency and Disclosure
references.note: Senior management must ensure staff and intermediaries, especially those who sell or market financial products, are adequately trained on and know the disclosure requirements for those products.

programs.title: Malaysia | Complaints Handling
programs.why: Under the new complaints handling policy document, effective 1 April 2026, staff in the complaints function must receive adequate and continuous training on the bank's procedures so they can assess complaints fairly and deal professionally with diverse and vulnerable consumers. The FTFC policy document also requires senior management to ensure complaints staff are properly trained.

references.title: Policy Document on Complaints Handling
references.note: Staff of the complaints handling function must be empowered to resolve complaints and receive adequate and continuous training on complaints procedures, including handling vulnerable consumers.

references.title: Policy Document on Fair Treatment of Financial Consumers
references.note: Senior management must ensure staff are properly trained to handle and resolve complaints and claims.

programs.title: Malaysia | Financial Markets Ombudsman Service Referrals
programs.why: Banks must belong to an approved financial ombudsman scheme and must refer eligible unresolved complaints to the Financial Markets Ombudsman Service, or otherwise to BNMLINK. Staff need to know when and how to signpost these routes.

references.title: Financial Services Act 2013
references.note: Requires financial service providers to be members of an approved financial ombudsman scheme.

references.title: Policy Document on Complaints Handling
references.note: Banks must refer eligible complainants to FMOS and, where FMOS has no jurisdiction and no referral is agreed, to BNMLINK.

programs.title: Malaysia | Mis-selling Prevention and Fair Dealing
programs.why: The FTFC policy document requires banks to put in place measures, including training, supervision and monitoring, so that staff, representatives and agents do not mislead consumers about products. Prohibited business conduct rules ban misleading or high-pressure sales practices.

references.title: Policy Document on Fair Treatment of Financial Consumers
references.note: Banks must use training, supervision and monitoring to stop staff, representatives and agents misleading consumers.

references.title: Policy Document on Prohibited Business Conduct
references.note: Specifies conduct that financial service providers and their sales and marketing representatives must not engage in, such as misleading or pressuring consumers during sales.

programs.title: Malaysia | Vulnerable Consumers
programs.why: From 1 April 2025, banks must give staff, representatives and agents, particularly those who interact with vulnerable consumers, the training needed to recognise, assess and respond to their needs. Guidance suggests internal programmes, practical guides and periodic refreshers.

references.title: Policy Document on Fair Treatment of Financial Consumers
references.note: Staff who interact with vulnerable consumers must be trained to recognise and respond to their needs; guidance suggests refresher training.

programs.title: Malaysia | Customer Information Secrecy (FSA Section 133 and BNM MCIPD)
programs.why: Section 133 of the Financial Services Act forbids disclosure of customer information outside permitted exceptions. BNM's 2025 policy document requires a high degree of staff awareness, training and regular reminders on confidentiality, specific training for new staff, effectiveness checks, and regular training by outsourced service providers.

references.title: Financial Services Act 2013
references.note: Prohibits directors, officers, agents and others from disclosing customer information except as permitted.

references.title: Policy Document on Management of Customer Information and Permitted Disclosures
references.note: Requires staff awareness, training and reminders on customer information confidentiality, induction training for new staff, ways to gauge training effectiveness and regular training by outsourced providers.

programs.title: Malaysia | Sales Advice and Suitability (FTFC and SC Capital Market Rules)
audience: Employees of registered persons dealing in capital market products
programs.why: BNM requires staff giving advice to be adequately trained and competent to recommend suitable products. Bank employees who carry on capital market activities as employees of a registered person must earn 20 CPE points a year under SC rules, and SC conduct guidelines require continuous training of representatives.

references.title: Policy Document on Fair Treatment of Financial Consumers
references.note: Staff, representatives and agents must be adequately trained and competent to give quality advice and understand key product features.

references.title: Guidelines on Compliance with the Continuing Professional Education Requirement (SC-GL/4-2018)
references.note: Employees of registered persons, which include banks carrying on capital market activities, must earn 20 CPE points a year to keep carrying on the regulated activity; the bank must determine their training needs and monitor compliance.

references.title: Guidelines on Conduct for Capital Market Intermediaries (SC-GL/3-2021, R2-2024)
references.note: Capital market intermediaries, including registered persons such as banks, must ensure representatives are competent, undertake continuous training, and are trained to identify and respond to vulnerable clients.

programs.title: Malaysia | Technology and Cybersecurity Awareness Education (RMiT)
programs.why: RMiT requires adequate, regular technology and cybersecurity awareness education for all staff, delivered at least annually and updated for evolving threats, with effectiveness measured; third-party providers should be included where appropriate.

references.title: Policy Document on Risk Management in Technology (RMiT)
references.note: All staff must receive technology and cybersecurity awareness education at least annually, and its effectiveness must be measured.

programs.title: Malaysia | Cybersecurity Awareness for Staff and NCII Entities
programs.why: Beyond the annual RMiT awareness duty, banks designated as national critical information infrastructure under the Cyber Security Act 2024 must follow the code of practice in RMiT Appendix 12, which requires a documented awareness plan covering cyber hygiene and social engineering, training of new employees before they access systems, and annual review of the programme.

references.title: Policy Document on Risk Management in Technology (RMiT)
references.note: Annual cybersecurity awareness for all staff; NCII entities must also train new employees before granting access and review the programme yearly.

programs.title: Malaysia | Training for Technology, Cybersecurity and Risk Staff (RMiT)
programs.why: RMiT requires adequate and continuous training for staff involved in technology operations, cybersecurity and risk management, so that they are competent and suitably certified for their roles.

references.title: Policy Document on Risk Management in Technology (RMiT)
references.note: Staff in technology operations, cybersecurity and risk management must receive continuous training and be competent and suitably certified.

programs.title: Malaysia | Personal Data Protection Act 2010 (as amended in 2024)
programs.why: The PDPA principles apply to banks as data controllers. The Security Principle requires steps to ensure the reliability, integrity and competence of personnel who access personal data, and since June 2025 controllers and processors must appoint a data protection officer. The Act does not prescribe staff training.

references.title: Personal Data Protection Act 2010 (Act 709), Reprint as at 15 September 2026
references.note: Requires measures to ensure the reliability and competence of personnel with access to personal data, and the appointment of data protection officers.

references.title: Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Act 2024 (Act A1727)
references.note: Commissioner's page on the 2024 amendments; not opened because the host refused automated access.

programs.title: Malaysia | Phishing, Scams and Social Engineering
programs.why: RMiT requires secure customer communication channels to reduce phishing, and the NCII code requires awareness plans to cover social engineering. The unauthorised e-banking policy document requires customer service staff to stay aware of current fraud and scam risks. A specific phishing course is not prescribed for all banks.

references.title: Policy Document on Risk Management in Technology (RMiT)
references.note: Banks must adopt channels resistant to phishing; NCII entities' awareness plans must cover social engineering.

references.title: Policy Document on Ensuring Fair Treatment for Victims of Unauthorised e-Banking Transactions
references.note: Customer service personnel must be kept well aware of current fraud risks and the bank's fraud investigation process so they can advise customers on frauds, scams and identity theft; banks must also regularly remind customers of safety tips.

programs.title: Malaysia | Cyber Incident Notification to BNM
audience: IT security and incident response teams
programs.why: RMiT requires banks to notify BNM of cyber incidents under the BCM and operational risk reporting policy documents; the BCM document sets a two-hour notification window after confirmation. Incident teams must be competent to identify and escalate incidents in time.

references.title: Policy Document on Risk Management in Technology (RMiT)
references.note: Banks must notify BNM of cyber incidents in line with the operational risk reporting and BCM policy documents.

references.title: Policy Document on Business Continuity Management
references.note: Senior management must make sure staff at every level are equipped for their BCM roles, and BCP testing must assess staff familiarity with their continuity duties; cyber incidents must be notified to BNM within two hours of confirmation.

programs.title: Malaysia | Customer Information Breach Management and Notification
programs.why: BNM requires all staff to understand breach escalation procedures, relevant staff to be trained on remedial actions and on handling affected customers' queries, and immediate notification to BNM of significant breaches. Under the amended PDPA, data controllers must notify the Commissioner as soon as practicable and affected individuals where significant harm is likely.

references.title: Policy Document on Management of Customer Information and Permitted Disclosures
references.note: All staff must understand escalation procedures; relevant staff must be trained on remediation and on handling affected customers; significant breaches must be notified to BNM immediately.

references.title: Personal Data Protection Act 2010 (Act 709), Reprint as at 15 September 2026
references.note: Data controllers must notify the Commissioner of personal data breaches as soon as practicable, and data subjects where significant harm is likely.

programs.title: Malaysia | Technology Risk Management (RMiT)
programs.why: RMiT sets board, senior management and operational requirements for technology risk, cybersecurity, cloud and digital services. It was reissued in 2025 and again in September 2026 with a code of practice for NCII-designated banks, superseding earlier e-banking fraud specifications.

references.title: Policy Document on Risk Management in Technology (RMiT)
references.note: Sets the technology risk framework and lists the earlier RMiT and e-banking fraud instruments it supersedes.

programs.title: Malaysia | Risk Governance and Enterprise Risk Awareness (BNM)
programs.why: BNM's Risk Governance policy document requires the board to build and keep risk management knowledge through continuing education and training, senior management to have the right risk skills, and the institution to promote risk awareness among all staff so that risk is part of everyday decisions.

references.title: Policy Document on Risk Governance
references.note: The board must keep, including through continuing education and training, enough risk management knowledge to oversee senior management, and the institution must promote awareness of risk across all staff.

programs.title: Malaysia | Operational Risk Management and ORR Reporting
programs.why: The Operational Risk policy document places operational risk ownership with business lines and requires the board to understand major operational risks; no separate course is prescribed. Since January 2026 the ORR policy document sets detailed loss event, fraud and KRI reporting that staff must capture accurately.

references.title: Policy Document on Operational Risk
references.note: The board must understand the major operational risks, and business lines own operational risk management with staff given the authority and resources to carry it out.

references.title: Policy Document on Operational Risk Reporting (ORR)
references.note: Sets the loss event, fraud and key risk indicator data that institutions must report to BNM and the reporting deadlines; it replaced the April 2025 version.

programs.title: Malaysia | Credit Risk Management (BNM Credit Risk Policy Document)
programs.why: The 2024 Credit Risk policy document requires a bank to set and carry out an internal policy on training and continuing professional development for officers with credit risk responsibilities, in both business lines and control functions, and encourages accredited credit risk qualifications.

references.title: Policy Document on Credit Risk
references.note: Institutions must set and implement an internal policy on training and continuing professional development for officers with credit risk responsibilities in business and control functions; accredited credit risk qualifications are encouraged.

programs.title: Malaysia | Liquidity Risk Management, LCR and NSFR
programs.why: Under the Liquidity Risk policy document in force from 15 October 2025, internal controls over liquidity risk must be run by independent officers who are appropriately trained and competent. Treasury and finance staff also need working knowledge of the LCR and NSFR calculations.

references.title: Policy Document on Liquidity Risk
references.note: Senior management must give responsibility for liquidity risk internal controls to operationally independent officers who are appropriately trained and competent.

references.title: Policy Document on Liquidity Coverage Ratio
references.note: Sets the LCR calculation, the stock of high-quality liquid assets and the outflow and inflow assumptions banks must apply.

references.title: Policy Document on Net Stable Funding Ratio
references.note: Sets the available and required stable funding factors used to compute the NSFR.

programs.title: Malaysia | Capital Adequacy Framework and ICAAP
programs.why: BNM's Capital Adequacy Framework sets capital components, risk-weighted asset rules and the ICAAP; it calls for qualified independent review of the ICAAP but no specific training. Staff who compute or oversee capital ratios need competence in these rules.

references.title: Capital Adequacy Framework (Capital Components)
references.note: Defines the eligibility criteria for CET1, Additional Tier 1 and Tier 2 capital, regulatory adjustments and minimum capital ratios.

references.title: Capital Adequacy Framework (Basel II - Risk-Weighted Assets)
references.note: Sets how credit, market and operational risk-weighted assets are calculated for the capital ratios.

references.title: Risk-Weighted Capital Adequacy Framework (Basel II) - Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process (Pillar 2)
references.note: The ICAAP must be reviewed independently by qualified functions that are not involved in designing or running it.

programs.title: Malaysia | Stress Testing (BNM Policy Document)
programs.why: The Stress Testing policy document requires the board to approve the programme, make sure there is sufficient expertise and challenge results, and requires independent review by a qualified party. This is a competence expectation rather than a training rule.

references.title: Policy Document on Stress Testing
references.note: The board must approve the stress testing programme, make sure it has enough expertise and challenge results; independent reviews must be done by a qualified party not involved in the programme.

programs.title: Malaysia | Outsourcing Risk Management
programs.why: BNM's outsourcing policy document requires board approval and oversight of material outsourcing and controls on service providers. The customer information policy document separately requires outsourced providers to train their personnel regularly on handling customer information.

references.title: Policy Document on Outsourcing
references.note: Sets board and senior management duties to approve, assess and monitor material outsourcing arrangements and the contractual safeguards required from service providers and their staff.

references.title: Policy Document on Management of Customer Information and Permitted Disclosures
references.note: Banks must make outsourced service providers train their personnel at regular intervals on handling customer information.

programs.title: Malaysia | Business Continuity Management
programs.why: BNM's BCM policy document requires senior management to make sure all levels of staff are equipped for their continuity roles, and BCP testing must check staff familiarity with their responsibilities and evacuation procedures. Disaster recovery testing rules applied from December 2025.

references.title: Policy Document on Business Continuity Management
references.note: Senior management must make sure staff at every level are equipped for their BCM roles, and BCP testing must assess staff familiarity with their continuity duties; cyber incidents must be notified to BNM within two hours of confirmation.

programs.title: Malaysia | Recovery Planning (BNM Policy Document)
programs.why: BNM's Recovery Planning policy document requires clear recovery roles for the board, management and business units and a governing body of personnel with the necessary competencies, so that recovery options can be carried out under stress.

references.title: Policy Document on Recovery Planning
references.note: Institutions must define recovery planning roles for the board, management and business units, and the board must appoint a senior officer and a governing body of personnel with the necessary competencies to drive the process.

programs.title: Malaysia | Responsible Personal Financing and Affordability
programs.why: The Personal Financing policy document (September 2025) requires suitability and affordability checks, caps tenure and bans flat-rate and Rule of 78 pricing, read with the Responsible Financing policy document of the same date, whose text could not be located on BNM's site. No staff training duty is stated.

references.title: Policy Document on Personal Financing
references.note: Requires suitability and affordability assessment before personal financing is granted, caps tenure at 10 years and bans flat-rate and Rule of 78 interest methods; some parts apply from 1 January 2027.

programs.title: Malaysia | Impaired Loans: Collection and Disposal
programs.why: The 2024 policy document on disposal and purchase of impaired loans requires buyers to have competent, qualified or trained collection staff and non-bank buyers to train staff on borrower information; banks selling loans must check these conditions.

references.title: Policy Document on Disposal and Purchase of Impaired Loans/Financing
references.note: A buyer of impaired loans must have competent, qualified or trained collection staff, and a non-bank buyer must train and regularly remind staff with access to borrower information on handling it with care.

programs.title: Malaysia | MFRS 9 Impairment and Regulatory Reserves (BNM Financial Reporting)
programs.why: BNM's Financial Reporting policy document adds prudential rules to MFRS 9: a 1% floor for loss allowance plus regulatory reserves, a 90-day credit-impaired test and rules for restructured loans. Staff who classify loans or compute provisions need competence in these rules; no course is prescribed.

references.title: Policy Document on Financial Reporting
references.note: Banks applying MFRS 9 must hold loss allowance on non-credit-impaired exposures plus regulatory reserves of at least 1% of credit exposures, and must classify facilities as credit-impaired when more than 90 days past due; restructured impaired loans stay impaired until conditions are met.

programs.title: Malaysia | Credit Bureau Reporting (CCRIS)
programs.why: Section 47 of the Central Bank of Malaysia Act lets BNM run a credit bureau using information supplied by financial institutions and shared under secrecy. Accurate reporting and proper use of the data call for staff competence; no training duty is stated.

references.title: Central Bank of Malaysia Act 2009 (Act 701)
references.note: BNM runs a credit bureau that collects credit information from financial institutions and may share it with institutions, the customer concerned and registered credit reporting agencies (the latter with customer consent), all under secrecy.

programs.title: Malaysia | Dormant Accounts and Unclaimed Moneys
programs.why: Banks must transfer long-unclaimed balances to the Registrar under the Unclaimed Moneys Act 1965. The official text on the Accountant General's site could not be opened from this session, so no staff duty was verified and the program is good practice only.

references.title: Unclaimed Moneys Act 1965 (Act 370), English text
references.note: Requires banks to pay balances unclaimed for the statutory period to the Registrar of Unclaimed Moneys; the Accountant General's site could not be opened through this session's network.

programs.title: Malaysia | Interoperable Fund Transfer Framework (DuitNow and shared infrastructure)
programs.why: The Interoperable Fund Transfer Framework (30 June 2026) replaced the 2019 Interoperable Credit Transfer Framework. It requires operators to staff participant oversight with competent people and encourages them to train participants on the scheme rules.

references.title: Policy Document on Interoperable Fund Transfer Framework
references.note: Replaces the 2019 Interoperable Credit Transfer Framework; operators of shared payment infrastructure should train participants on the rules and must staff participant oversight with skilled, competent people.

programs.title: Malaysia | Credit and Debit Card Requirements (BNM 2025 Policy Documents)
programs.why: The December 2025 credit card and debit card policy documents require issuers to train front-line staff to explain minimum payment rules and to make sure sales, telemarketing and customer service staff are trained in card features, benefits and risks.

references.title: Policy Document on Credit Card and Credit Card-i
references.note: Issuers must train front-line staff to explain minimum payment requirements to cardholders and make sure sales and telemarketing staff are trained in the key features, benefits and risks of card products.

references.title: Policy Document on Debit Card and Debit Card-i
references.note: Issuers must make sure sales and customer service staff, including call centres, are adequately trained on the features, benefits and risks of debit cards.

references.title: Policy Document on Payment Cards Framework
references.note: Sets interchange fee ceilings, routing choice for merchants and other market practices for debit and credit card payments.

programs.title: Malaysia | E-Money Issuance (BNM E-Money Policy Document)
programs.why: The e-money policy document requires issuers to raise customer awareness and give annual cybersecurity awareness to staff, but a bank that issues e-money follows RMiT for the technology parts, so for banks the training duty sits in RMiT and this program is a competence need.

references.title: Policy Document on Electronic Money (E-Money)
references.note: E-money issuers must educate customers and give staff at least annual cybersecurity awareness education; issuers that are banks follow RMiT for the technology requirements instead.

programs.title: Malaysia | Remittance and Money-Changing by Banks
programs.why: BNM's requirements for money services business conducted by banks expressly require adequate ongoing training for staff and appointed agents on the rules and on AML/CFT duties such as CDD, record keeping and suspicious transaction reporting.

references.title: Policy Document on Requirements for the Conduct of Money Services Business by Banking Institutions
references.note: Banks conducting remittance or money-changing business must give staff and appointed agents adequate ongoing training on the policy document and AML/CFT duties such as CDD, record keeping and suspicious transaction reporting.

programs.title: Malaysia | Foreign Exchange Policy Notices
programs.why: BNM's Foreign Exchange Policy Notices (November 2024) set which foreign exchange transactions residents and non-residents may carry out and what banks must check; they state no training duty, but staff applying them need working knowledge.

references.title: Foreign Exchange Policy Notices
references.note: Consolidated notices on currency dealings, borrowing and lending, foreign currency assets, payments, securities, cash movement and export proceeds; they revoked the June 2022 notices.

programs.title: Malaysia | Sexual Harassment Awareness (Employment Act 1955)
programs.why: Since 1 January 2023, section 81H of the Employment Act requires every employer to display a notice at the workplace at all times to raise awareness of sexual harassment, alongside the employer's duty to inquire into complaints. The Act requires awareness but does not set a training course or frequency.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265), Reprint as at 1 August 2023
references.note: Employers must always display a conspicuous notice at the workplace to raise awareness of sexual harassment; Part XVA also governs complaints and inquiries.

programs.title: Malaysia | Prudential Reporting and Data Quality
programs.why: BNM's data management and MIS guidelines expect data stewards to protect the integrity of information reported to BNM and to support users with training and manuals; reporting rules such as ORR add detailed submissions. This is a competence expectation.

references.title: Guidelines on Data Management and MIS Framework
references.note: Data stewardship roles include protecting the integrity of financial information reported to BNM and giving users continuing development support, including training and user manuals.

references.title: Policy Document on Operational Risk Reporting (ORR)
references.note: Sets the loss event, fraud and key risk indicator data that institutions must report to BNM and the reporting deadlines; it replaced the April 2025 version.

programs.title: Malaysia | FATCA Compliance
programs.why: Malaysian banks report US account information to the Inland Revenue Board for exchange with the US. Staff must collect self-certifications and apply due diligence correctly. The official pages could not be opened because the host refused automated access.

references.title: Automatic Exchange of Information (AEOI)
references.note: LHDN pages on automatic exchange of financial account information, including FATCA and CRS; not opened because the host refused automated access.

programs.title: Malaysia | Common Reporting Standard (CRS)
programs.why: CRS obligations apply to Malaysian financial institutions through the Income Tax (Automatic Exchange of Financial Account Information) Rules 2016, including self-certification and residence due diligence. LHDN's pages could not be opened because the host refused automated access, so this entry is based on search results only.

references.title: Common Reporting Standard (CRS)
references.note: LHDN guidance and rules on CRS due diligence and reporting; not opened because the host refused automated access.

programs.title: Malaysia | Capital Market Products and SC Representative Competence
audience: Bank staff dealing in capital market products
programs.why: SC conduct guidelines require intermediaries, including banks as registered persons, to make sure representatives are competent and undergo continuous training, and the SC CPE guidelines set the points representatives must earn.

references.title: Guidelines on Conduct for Capital Market Intermediaries (SC-GL/3-2021, R2-2024)
references.note: Intermediaries, including registered persons such as banks, must make sure representatives are authorised or registered, competent, and keep their knowledge current through continuous training.

references.title: Guidelines on Compliance with the Continuing Professional Education Requirement (SC-GL/4-2018)
references.note: Sets the annual CPE points that licensed and registered representatives must earn to keep their status.

programs.title: Malaysia | Insider Trading and Market Misconduct
programs.why: The CMSA prohibits market manipulation and insider trading, and BNM's wholesale market code bars manipulation and insider dealing and expressly requires trade surveillance staff to be trained adequately to detect misconduct.

references.title: Policy Document on Code of Conduct for Malaysia Wholesale Financial Markets
references.note: Market participants, including licensed banks, must avoid manipulation and insider dealing, train trade surveillance staff to spot misconduct, and acquire technical and conduct training on an ongoing basis.

references.title: Capital Markets and Services Act 2007 (Act 671)
references.provision: Part V (market misconduct, including insider trading from section 183)
references.note: Prohibits market manipulation, false trading and dealing in or passing on inside information. The SC copy opened incorporates amendments only up to 28 December 2012.

programs.title: Malaysia | Code of Conduct for Wholesale Financial Markets
programs.why: BNM's Code of Conduct for Malaysia Wholesale Financial Markets requires market participants to acquire technical and conduct training on an ongoing basis and expects management to train all staff involved in wholesale market activities.

references.title: Policy Document on Code of Conduct for Malaysia Wholesale Financial Markets
references.note: Market participants, including licensed banks, must avoid manipulation and insider dealing, train trade surveillance staff to spot misconduct, and acquire technical and conduct training on an ongoing basis.

programs.title: Malaysia | Electronic Know-Your-Customer (e-KYC)
programs.why: The 2024 e-KYC policy document requires board approval of the e-KYC risk appetite and framework and ongoing oversight of its effectiveness; staff running remote onboarding need competence in the controls, but no training is prescribed.

references.title: Policy Document on Electronic Know-Your-Customer (e-KYC)
references.note: The board must approve the risk appetite and framework for e-KYC and oversee its effectiveness, including false acceptance rate monitoring and certification of solution modules where available.

programs.title: Malaysia | Fintech Regulatory Sandbox and Fintech Partnerships
programs.why: BNM's sandbox framework covers financial institutions and the fintech companies working with them, and requires participants to commit adequate and competent resources to testing within set safeguards.

references.title: Policy Document on Financial Technology Regulatory Sandbox Framework
references.note: Applies to financial institutions and the fintech companies that partner with them; participants must commit adequate and competent resources to test solutions under BNM's conditions.

programs.title: Malaysia | AI Governance in Financial Services
programs.why: BNM's August 2025 discussion paper on AI sets out proposed expectations on governance, validation and fairness of AI, including approval by a competent internal party. It is not yet binding, so training is good practice.

references.title: Discussion Paper on Artificial Intelligence in the Malaysian Financial Sector
references.note: Sets out proposed expectations on AI governance, including approval of AI use by a competent internal party, testing and validation of models, fairness and data quality; not yet binding.

programs.title: Malaysia | Open Finance (Proposed BNM Framework)
programs.why: BNM consulted on an open finance framework in November 2025, covering consent-based data sharing through standard APIs. Until a final policy document is issued, training is good practice only.

references.title: Exposure Draft on Open Finance
references.note: Proposed requirements for data sharing through standardised APIs with customer consent; comments closed on 1 March 2026 and the final policy document was not yet seen.

notes: AMLA was amended by Act A1761 (gazetted 14 May 2025, in force 1 March 2026): it is renamed to add Anti-Restricted Activity Financing, extends compliance programme and CDD duties to directors, officers and employees personally, and lets BNM issue binding instructions on compliance programmes. The consolidated LOM text dated 1 July 2022 does not yet include these changes.
The AML/CFT/CPF and TFS for FIs policy document took effect on 6 February 2024, replacing the 2019 AML/CFT and TFS for FIs document and adding proliferation financing.

The PDPA was amended by Act A1727 in three stages during 2025; data protection officer and breach notification duties (sections 12A and 12B) took effect on 1 June 2025. LOM published a reprint as at 15 September 2026.

RMiT was revised with effect from 28 November 2025 and reissued on 25 September 2026 with a code of practice for NCII entities under the Cyber Security Act 2024; it supersedes the e-banking guidelines, earlier fraud specifications and the 2023 RMiT.
The Management of Customer Information and Permitted Disclosures policy document was reissued on 31 October 2025, replacing the 2023 version.
A new Complaints Handling policy document takes effect on 1 April 2026 (FMOS referral rules applied from 28 March 2025), replacing the 2009 guidelines.

Responsibility Mapping took effect on 1 January 2026; the FTFC vulnerable consumer provisions applied from 1 April 2025; Product Transparency and Disclosure (December 2024) phases in during 2025-2026.
BNM issued Personal Financing and Responsible Financing policy documents on 30 September 2025 and a discussion paper on operational resilience in December 2025.
Islamic banking requirements under IFSA 2013 and Shariah governance are out of scope for this map.

Breadth update: the Interoperable Fund Transfer Framework (30 June 2026) replaced the 2019 Interoperable Credit Transfer Framework; the ORR policy document was reissued on 30 January 2026; new credit and debit card policy documents (19 December 2025) phase in until 1 January 2027; the Liquidity Risk policy document applied from 15 October 2025; open finance (November 2025) and IRRBB (September 2025) exposure drafts are pending.
